hunts.label: Saturday, Oct 31
hunts.subtitle: Halloween morning. The only thing in the woods that should spook you is a good shot chance.

rules.title: Clocks fall back tomorrow night
items: Clocks go back one hour at **2:00 am Sunday, Nov 1**. Saturday morning is still daylight time. Every time on this page is the clock you will see Saturday.
Sunday morning, sunrise is about 6:30 am and legal light about 6:00 am by the new clock. Your body will think it is an hour later.
Hunter orange is required (gun deer season, Oct 17 to Jan 1). Hat and vest on.
rules.note: Set your alarm for Saturday only. Check your phone shows the right time Sunday before you plan anything.

conditions.source: Source: National Weather Service point forecast, issued 8:00 pm Thursday. Sun times from sunrise-sunset.org.
items: **Walk-in, 5:30 am:** low near 49°F. Mostly clear. Calm early, then a light north breeze.
**Wind later in the day:** northeast at 6 to 10 mph. **High:** near 66°F.
**Moon:** waning gibbous, about 58% lit. Past full, still bright.
conditions.meaning: **What it likely means (my assumption, not proven):** a clear cool morning with a light breeze is quiet and good for scent control. A bright late moon may keep deer feeding late, so movement may run later than usual, 7:15 to 9:00. Sign should be fresh and the leaves are dry, so every step is loud. Move slowly.

wind.label: from the N to NE, light, about 5 to 8 mph (estimate for dawn)

in_season: **Deer, either sex** (gun season, day 15). Pre-rut: bucks are starting to cruise.

in_season.tip: Needs your HIP number and the 3-shell plug. Check the Digest for the shot rule before you shoot one. If unsure, just look.
Opportunity only. Shoot one only if a crow commits over your sit.

in_season.text: Awareness only: rails, gallinules, bobcat and bear
in_season.tip: Rails and gallinules are open but the swamp is poor habitat. Bobcat is open. Bear is closed until Nov 14. You are not hunting any of these. Carry the slugs for defense only.

in_season: Ducks, dove and woodcock are closed today. Ducks and dove reopen Nov 7.

plan.title: The plan: a new sit at the middle pinch of the main trail
plan.why: **Why here:** deer cross the property from the SE pasture side toward the swamp thickets, and the center is where the main trail and the loop trail come closest. A light N to NE wind sends your scent SW and S, behind you, away from deer coming from the east and north. This also teaches you the middle of the land, which you have not sat yet. **Timing:** legal light is 6:59, so you want to be seated by about 6:15. That means leaving the yard at 5:30, not 4:30. A long wait in the cold only makes you fidget.

steps.text: Leave the yard on the main trail, heading NE. Red light low. Dry leaves are loud. Walk slowly: three steps, listen, three steps.

Find the pinch: the place in the middle of the woods where the main trail and the loop trail pass closest. Step off the trail to the WEST about 25 yards. Pick a pine or holly trunk wider than your shoulders.
Sit with your back to the trunk. Cushion down. Face NE. Your view should cover the trail pinch and the woods north and east. Check there is no house, field or yard behind any lane you may shoot.
Load at the sit. Muzzle points N or E. Safety on. Thread test: tie a 12-inch thread on the barrel to see the real wind.
Legal light. Watch east and north. Deer move along the trail edges. Look for ears and legs, not whole deer.
No deer? Stay. Bucks cruise late in the pre-rut. Count to 100 slowly twice before you move.
Swap 00 for #4. Walk the loop trail east then south for squirrel. Squirrels feed on the ground after the sun dries the leaves.
Build the brush blind (see the Skill tab) at the sit or a thick edge near it. Practice only. Shoot nothing while you build.
Walk out. Unload at the yard edge. Log what you saw with a "note:" message.

items: **In the gun:** 00 buckshot in the magazine. Modified choke. Safety on.
**Right pocket:** #4 and #7.5 birdshot. Swap in at about 8:30.
**Also carry:** knife, hatchet (for the blind), gloves, 12-inch thread, dry layer, cushion.
warnings: Never shoot a deer with birdshot.
Never shoot buckshot or slugs without the ground behind the target.
Keep buckshot and birdshot in different pockets. Check by feel.

animals.name: Deer
paragraphs: **Local:** common. They bed in the swamp thickets and feed in the SE pasture and the mast areas.
**Today:** pre-rut. Bucks start looking for does. Best windows (assumption): 7:00 to 8:00 and again 8:30 to 9:00 as the air warms.
**Shot:** broadside or quartering away only. 30 yards maximum with 00. Aim behind the front shoulder, middle of the body. Shoot only to the N, NE, E or W. Never south.

details.title: Skill: read the tail and ears before you shoot
paragraphs: **Relaxed:** tail down or lazy swish, head low, ears forward and moving. You have time. Wait for the best angle.
**Alert:** head up, ears locked on you, tail slightly raised. Freeze. Do not blink if you can help it. Wait it out.
**Danger:** a foot stomp, a snort, the white tail flagged high. The deer is gone. Do not take a running shot with 00.
A walking deer pauses when it hears something odd. That pause is your shot window, if the angle is right.
details.note: A doe often leads. Hold five minutes after she passes. A buck may be tracking her with his nose down.

details.title: Technique: wait for the second deer
steps: When one deer passes, stay still and count to 60.
Deer travel in groups. A second or third is often behind.
Do not move your gun until the lead deer is fully out of sight.

after: **Tip:** you see ears flick before you see a deer. Scan the same lane slowly, left to right, every minute.
**Tip:** report any harvest as the NCWRC Regulations Digest describes.

animals.name: Squirrel
paragraphs: **Local:** gray squirrels seen often. Fox squirrel is possible.
**Today:** after 8:30 the sun dries the bark and leaves. Squirrels drop to the ground to feed. (Assumption.)
**Shot:** head and neck. #4 to 30 yards. #7.5 to 25 yards.

details.title: Technique: hear the rhythm
steps: In dry leaves, stop every few steps and listen.
A squirrel makes a short, steady rustle: dig, pause, dig.
A deer or a wind gust is random and heavier. Wait for the rhythm.
Look 20 to 30 yards toward the sound, low, near trunks and fallen limbs.

after: **Tip:** shoot only with a trunk, the ground or water behind the squirrel. Never toward the house.

animals.name: Rabbit
paragraphs: **Local:** likely at the feed bins and the thick edges.

details.title: Call: the squeak stop
steps: When a rabbit runs, make a sharp squeak: suck air hard through pursed lips against the back of your hand.
A running rabbit often stops and sits up to look.
Shoot while it is stopped, N, E or W only.

after: **Safety:** wear gloves when you handle it. Check the liver (last week's Skill tab).

animals.name: Raccoon and opossum
paragraphs: Opportunity only. A dawn den return near the bins is possible. The same shot rules apply. Do not shoot toward the house or field.

animals.name: Snipe
paragraphs: **Local:** possible on soft mud near the beaver lodge. A low-odds extra.
**Rule:** needs your HIP number and the 3-shell plug. Check the Digest for the shot rule first. If you cannot confirm it, skip the shot.

details.title: Technique: look before you walk
steps: From the edge, scan the wet mud for a long bill probing.
Snipe freeze, then burst up with a raspy "scaipe" call.
Mark where it flushes and do not shoot toward the south.

after: **Tip:** only check on the walk out, after 8:30. Do not walk the mud at the sit time.

animals.name: Crow
paragraphs: **Local:** common flyers over the pasture and swamp. Saturday is an open day.
**Today:** opportunity only. Stand still against a trunk.

details.title: Technique: shoot the committing bird
steps: Crows flare at movement. Keep your face down until a bird is within range.
Shoot one that is gliding in with its wings cupped, not one passing high.
#4 shot, 30 yards or less.

skill.title: Skill of the week: build a ten-minute brush blind
skill.principle: **Core principle:** break up your outline and hide your movement. You do not need a stand or a blind kit. You need a solid background behind you and cover in front. Use only dead, fallen material. Do not cut live trees.

sections.title: Build it
steps: Pick a spot where a thick trunk or a wall of brush sits directly behind you. Never sit in the open with sky behind you.
Decide your lanes first: N, NE and E (or W). Clear a lane about 2 yards wide at head and shoulder height. Leave the ground in front intact for a backstop.
Gather dead limbs, pine boughs and leafy branches. Choose pieces 4 to 6 feet long.
Lean them upright, stuck into the ground, in a half circle on the SOUTH and WEST sides, about 3 feet away from you. This hides you from the side and rear.
Leave the front lanes open, with a few low branches so your legs are hidden.
Add loose branches overhead only if there is no tree above you.
Sit. Look out of each lane. Move your arms and gun. Trim anything that blocks you or snags the barrel.

sections.title: Check it
steps: Walk 30 yards away and look back. Can you see a human shape? If so, add cover at that height.
Make sure no lane points toward the house (SW) or the field (SE) or the south.

details.title: Tap to open: why the cover goes on the sides and back
paragraphs: Deer see movement far better than shape. A blind that hides your arms and your head turns lets you shift slowly without being seen. It also gives you a place to rest your elbows. Build it on the walk out today, so next week it is ready before you sit.

skill.checkpoint: **Checkpoint:** next week, sit in it before dawn and test it. Tell me with a "note:" message if the lanes worked.

land.intro: Learn the middle of the property. Make a simple map on the walk out.
steps: Draw a rough map on paper: yard, main trail, Junction, loop trail, feed bins, beaver lodge, thickest pine.
Pace the distance from the pinch to the Junction and from the pinch to the bins. Write the numbers on the map.
Mark every track or rub within 50 yards of the pinch.
Run the thread test at your sit at 6:15 and 8:15. Note which way the thread points.
Send a "note:" message with what you found. Next week's plan will use it.

safety: **Shooting arc:** north, northeast, east, northwest. NEVER south. The house is SW, the field is SE, the neighbor is south.
Buckshot and slugs need the ground behind them.
Hunter orange on. Hat and vest.
Cold at dawn, near 49°F. Bring a dry layer and gloves. Do not let your hands go numb on the gun.
Dry leaves and stumps are loud and can hide holes. Walk in the dark with the red light and watch your footing.
Bear and fox are in the area. Back away from any cub. Slugs are for defense only.
hunts.regs: Check the NCWRC Regulations Digest for deer reporting, bag limits, snipe and crow rules.
hunts.gaps: no hunting entries in your Daily Notes this week. The point forecast gives no hour-by-hour table for Saturday, so I left the hourly chart out. I could not find the Saturday moonrise or moonset. I could not confirm the shot-type rule for snipe, so it is marked check-first.
